newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended up on the day, although slightly off early morning highs, with almost all attention on the government's new 10 year benchmark.
"It seems there was about two billion (guilders) of turnover in the first hour (in the new issue) which should have made them quite happy," one trader said.
The new 5.75 percent February 2007 bonds were initially priced at 100.65 guilders and rapidly rose to 101.00, before the market ran out of steam.
At session close, banks priced the bonds at around 100.70, providing a yield of about 5.66.

The new issue created trading opportunities around the ten year part of the curve. A number of traders made or noticed switching from Jan 2006s and, to a lesser extent, from the current 8.25 percent February 2007s.
By the close of sales at 1600 GMT, the government had raise 3.6 billion guilders. The tap resumes on Tuesday from 0800 GMT.
Traders agreed that the government would need to sell 10-15 billion guilders worth for the paper to become a viable benchmark. However, there was no consensus as to the likely strategy.

Some traders believed the government would continue selling for at least another two days, hoping for larger midweek trading volumes. Others said it would raise an initial five to six billion guilders and then reopen the issue later in the year.
"Overall, the borrowing requirement is not that high, so they don't need to panic," one trader said.

In general, the market received an initial boost from bund strength. A number switched along the curve, principally at maturities of 2002, 2005 and 2006, but trading energy rapidly dissipated. The lack of U.S. market due to a public holiday left few opportunities in the afternoon.
